correctness.rationale: The truncated geometric family is strictly increasing in its parameter by exponential-family variance. For each k and n>2k the mean crosses integer k uniquely between r=k/(k+1) and 1; as n grows the ratio converges back to k/(k+1). Reflecting gives finite log-affine laws of integer mean n-k with tail probability approaching (k/(k+1))^k and finally e^-1. The published integer-mean corollary proves the opposite bound; numerical script only corroborates representative parameters.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Earlier stronger-looking theorems are checked at the level of their actual assumptions and conclusions; Alqasem–Aravinda–Marsiglietti–Melbourne 2023 arXiv full HTML Introduction Corollary 1.4 and Section 3 read: integer-mean e^-1 bound, unrestricted sharpness and the eight-atom violation of 1/2 are prior art. Their displayed sharpness family does not impose integer mean; the current exact integer-mean perturbation and double limit resolve a genuine subclass sharpness gap. Marsiglietti–Melbourne discrete localization establishes log-affine extremizers, but explicit integer-mean saturation was not found. An unindexed traditional tail construction remains possible.
